newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CIL says EBIT comfortably ahead in Q1.
newsitem.headline: CIL says EBIT comfortably ahead in Q1.

text.p: Corporate Investments Ltd Chief Executive Bryan Mogridge said on Thursday that the New Zealand investment company was on track to exceed its 1996/7 June year target for earnings before interest and tax (EBIT).
CIL was also "comfortably ahead" of last year's EBIT after completing the first quarter.
Most of its growth was expected to come from CIL's Montana Wines, he said. CIL's EBIT in 1995/6 was NZ$36.5 million.

Mogridge told the annual meeting that CIL's other main businesses, Truck Investments Ltd and Game Meats, planned to grow at only a modest pace, in line with conservative predictions for economic growth.

On CIL's 50 Cavill Avenue property in Surfers Paradise, he said there had been buyer interest in the company that owns the building "which may or may not translate into a sale". The building is 90 percent leased.
Overseas demand for Montana's wines was very strong, particularly in Britain and Australia and Montana had sufficient unused winery capacity to cope with increased production.

"This spare capacity avoids the need for major capital expenditure but will see Montana require at least NZ$4.5 million a year for vineyards and $5.0 million for the wineries to produce and process the extra premium wines to be sold.
"This investment will continue for the next 4-5 years, but if Montana continues to grow, further investment will be required," he said.
Premium wines required longer stock maturation than commercial wines, which uses up cash for working capital.
"Our cashflow plans show the group can manage this growth well within its own cashflow generated from profits," he said.
Interest bearing debt would also decrease with each year.

Mogridge saw the current oversupply of grapes as an opportunity, leading to lower grape prices and higher volumes and enabling Montana to meet so far unsatisfied export demand and underused winery capacity.
Chairman Peter Masfen said the group still had significant unused tax losses and tax pre-payments domiciled in New Zealand.
This meant there would be no tax liability on about NZ$55 million of future income.
The major portion of the tax benefit on about NZ$15 million, which had not been included in the June year balance sheet, would benefit the current year's profit, he said.
CIL was trading unchanged at $0.59, two cents below its high for the year and up from NZ$0.25 in June 1995.
